findings.summary: The timeout fresh-plan test could pass without checking anything.
findings.evidence: A retry of a timed-out job may resume from kept work through `timeout_seed` (run.rs:237-270). Planning still runs for every planned job (run.rs:539-542). The test still has to make sure the job really closed `timed_out` and that the retry reaches planning. Fix: Assert that the predecessor's state is Closed(TimedOut), and that the retry made a Planner call, before checking that the kept plan and findings are absent.
findings.location: Plan, Demonstrations, Criterion 2 (timeout case); crates/athena-core/src/run.rs:402-405 and 539-542

findings.summary: The call-order assertion is worded too broadly.
findings.evidence: After the critic, the run goes on to the producer and verifier, so 'exactly Planner then Critic' after the reader is only true for the planning calls. Fix: Assert that the planning calls, taken in order, are exactly [Planner, Critic] before the first Producer call.

findings.summary: The plan does not say how the predecessor chain is found.
findings.evidence: `retried_job` (reading.rs:1042) works out the predecessor from the request text. It is not a stored field. Fix: Say that the chain walk calls `crate::reading::retried_job(records, &request.text)` for each job, as steward.rs:385 does.

summary: I read the code; I ran nothing. The plan fits the request and the accepted reading, and the code it names exists. In run.rs, `plan_round` threads `revision: Option<PlanRevision>` into `planning_round`, so seeding round 1 is a small, well-placed change: one revision round, then the critic, under the same cap. `end_round` already pushes the round-3 plan and critique into `closing` before the cap stop, so reusing those records as the kept plan and findings is sound. `retried_job` is public, and `PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX` already exists in records.rs, so the new cap-reason const sits beside it. A grep for `JobPlan {` literals found the ones the plan names (admission.rs:488, store.rs:467, records.rs:3381, briefs.rs:1660) plus `plan_record` at run.rs:1266, which the plan also covers. So the two edits outside the listed files are forced and mechanical, as Athena's findings already note. The demonstrations check what the planner and the critic are actually given (prompt contents, the order of the planning calls, and the `resumed_from` marker), and each would fail without the behavior. The status measure is computed from records, with a before/after split taken from those records. My three findings are minor or nits, and none blocks the plan.
